notes: Emitted by the state writer rather than written by hand, which is the point of it. A node summary's decisions list carries both frozen object shapes and a bare string, and the writer spells an object entry as a block mapping opened on a sequence dash. That construct was legal to the schema, emitted by the writer and refused by the definition reader the rest of the runtime reads state through, so a run's summaries were unreadable to the collision guard that has to know which chain a run names. Both halves round-trip it now, and the suite reads this file through the writer's reader, the runtime's reader and a real YAML parser, holding the three to the same document.
